what: methodName / resourceName pairs that Google- and Elastic-authored GKE sources show, and probes of the regex grammar. The transform must produce each pair from the native objectRef, verb and response status; the pipeline's objectRef/verb regexes must hold on it, except the pair's 'lost' items, which must not hold (GKE does not record them). Each 'must_hold' probe must be true and each 'must_not_hold' probe false on the native Event and on its GKE transform. Each 'known_differences' probe is a documented loss of the GKE encoding: it must give its stated, different truth on each shape. Probe names are det-eng's (trr9007- markers); the probes that read kube-system keep that built-in namespace name because the CoreDNS rules key on objectRef.namespace: kube-system, and cluster-admin is the built-in binding that the Elastic rule names.

must_hold.why: the core group: objectRef.apiGroup is null (omitempty in audit.k8s.io/v1)
a namespace object is named by its own path
a namespace's finalize subresource names the namespace
a successful create names the created object

must_not_hold.why: a create in namespace kube-system is not an object named kube-system
a read of a configmap in namespace kube-system is not an object named kube-system
namespace kube-system is not namespace kube-system-trr9007 (no prefix match)
verb delete is not deletecollection (the verb is the last methodName label)
the resource of a pods/status patch is pods, not status
a group label (rbac) is not a subresource
group apps is not group apps.trr9007.example.com (no prefix match)
objectRef.apiGroup null is the core group only

known_differences.why: objectRef.namespace: X holds on GKE on the create of namespace X: resourceName core/v1/namespaces/<name> is both the namespace object and the namespace prefix, and a successful create names the created object. The native Event has no namespace there: kube-apiserver v1.36.4 requestinfo.go lines 194-196 set the namespace only from a path part after 'namespaces' (POST /api/v1/namespaces has none), and audit/request.go lines 130-131 fill it from the object's metadata.namespace, which a Namespace does not have
the same with a prefix: objectRef.namespace|startswith: trr9007 holds on GKE on the create of namespace trr9007-ns, not natively
